segments.text: Fourteen hundred years ago, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, described a scene... that reads like this morning's news. Nations, gathering around his people... the way hungry diners gather around a plate.
segments._shot: dark storm front rolling over a city skyline

segments.text: This is the prophecy... of the feast.
segments.title: THE FEAST
segments.titleSub: a prophecy of the Prophet, peace be upon him

segments.text: A prophecy, in Islam, is not a guess. Muslims believe the Prophet, peace be upon him, spoke of the future only by revelation from Allah... God Himself. And one day, he told his companions what was coming.
The nations will soon call one another against you... he said... the way diners call one another to a dish. Whole nations. One table. And his people... the meal.
Someone asked... will that be because we are few? He answered... no. You will be MANY on that day. But you will be like foam... like the froth a flood carries on its surface.
segments._shot: sea foam churning on dark water

segments.text: Numbers without weight. Presence without power. And then he named the reason. Allah will remove the fear of you from your enemies' chests... and cast into your hearts... al-wahn.
segments._shot: dust scattering in wind on dark ground

segments.text: They asked... what is al-wahn, O Messenger of Allah? He said... love of this world... and hatred of death.
segments._shot: city lights blurring out of focus at night

segments.text: Notice what he did not say. No year. No country. No enemy's name. He did not diagnose a nation... he diagnosed a heart. A heart so attached to this life that it cannot stand for anything beyond it.
segments._shot: single dim lamp in a large dark room

segments.text: And that means the prophecy carries its own cure. If the disease is loving this world too much... the cure is loving what lasts, more.
segments._shot: dawn light breaking over still water

segments.text: He saw this moment coming fourteen centuries away... and he told us, so we would not be foam. Hold your faith heavier than your fear. That is the whole answer... and it always was.
segments._shot: sunrise over a vast calm landscape
